prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: The story of the 2008 financial crisis, from the US housing boom to subprime mortgages, securitization, the fall of Lehman Brothers and the government response. A clear explanation of how a housing bubble nearly broke the global financial system.

beats.narration: A bet on ordinary American homes nearly broke the world economy. How did something as safe as a house become the spark for a global crisis?
It began with a housing boom. Interest rates were low, and prices kept climbing. Buying a home felt like a sure thing, so more and more people wanted in.

clip_queries: real estate sign in front yard

beats.narration: Lenders wanted to keep the boom going. So they offered subprime mortgages: loans to borrowers with weak credit, often with little checking and low starting payments.
Lenders did not worry much about repayment. Why? Because they did not plan to keep the loans. They sold them on to Wall Street.
There, banks bundled thousands of loans together and sliced them into securities. Investors around the world bought them. This is called securitization, and it spread the risk everywhere.
Rating agencies called many of these securities safe. Banks borrowed heavily to buy more of them. Everyone assumed house prices would never fall.

props.text: Everyone assumed house prices would never fall.

beats.narration: But prices did fall. Borrowers could not pay, and defaults rose. The securities lost value, and nobody knew which banks were holding the damage.
Then came Lehman Brothers, a major investment bank, which collapsed in September 2008. Panic spread. Banks stopped trusting each other, and lending froze.

props.image_query: Wall Street New York stock exchange

beats.narration: Governments stepped in. The US rescued banks and insurers with public money, and the central bank cut interest rates and pumped in cash to keep credit flowing.
The system survived, but millions lost jobs and homes. The lesson is simple: when risk is hidden and everyone shares the same bet, one weak spot can bring down everything.

props.text: Hidden risk, shared by everyone, can break everything.
